items.meta_title: Access Points: Your Servers' Addresses in VpnHood! MANAGER | VpnHood!
items.meta_description: Set the addresses a server listens on and puts in its access keys in VpnHood! MANAGER, on a cloud with private addresses too, and keep them out of the keys behind a reverse proxy.
items.title: Access points
items.lead: A server's access points are its addresses in VpnHood! MANAGER: the ones it listens on, and the ones that go into the access keys. MANAGER sets them by itself, until you need a particular address.
items.where_desc: Open [manager_servers], select the server and find its [manager_access_points]. Each access point is one address of the server, with its ports. The server farm's page lists the addresses its keys contain, under [manager_access_points] too.
items.auto_desc: [manager_auto_config] is on for every new server. MANAGER looks the server's address up through the server's own outgoing traffic, as a standalone server does, and sets the access points to match. That finds the right address on most machines; How the server finds its address lists when it does not.
items.auto_off: To set the access points yourself, turn [manager_auto_config] off: while it is on, the list cannot be changed. MANAGER asks you to confirm, because the server restarts with its new settings.
items.settings_fields: Two settings decide what each address is for:
items.set_mode: [manager_mode] decides who gets the address. [manager_public_in_token] puts it in every access key of the server farm. [manager_public] keeps it out of the keys, and MANAGER gives it to an app only when it sends that app to this server. [manager_private] never gives it to apps.
items.set_listen: [manager_listen] decides whether the server listens on the address. Set it to [manager_yes] only for an address your provider routes to the machine: on Linux, the server adds a listening address the machine does not have to its network by itself.
items.set_ports: [manager_udp_port] and [manager_quic_port] are optional, and [port_off] turns either off.
items.set_udp_open: Devices set to UDP need the server's [manager_udp_port] open too, in the machine's firewall and your hosting provider's.
items.shot_alt: The Access Points of a server in VpnHood! MANAGER, with Automatic Configuration off
items.shot_caption: The new address, [ip_connection_example], goes in the keys. The old one, [ip_outgoing_example], is kept out of them, but the server still listens on it for apps that hold an older key.
items.nat_title: On a cloud with private addresses
items.nat_desc: On a cloud where the machine has only private addresses, such as AWS, Google Cloud, Azure or Oracle Cloud, add the private address with [manager_mode] [manager_private] and [manager_listen] [manager_yes], and the public IP with [manager_public_in_token] and [manager_listen] [manager_no], on the same port. [manager_auto_config] sets up the same by itself.
items.change_desc: A key carries the addresses it was made with, so an app holding an older key keeps trying the old address. Keep the old one for a few days as an access point with [manager_mode] [manager_private] and [manager_listen] [manager_yes]: apps get the new key when they connect, because [manager_push_token] is on by default. Then remove it.
items.proxy_first: First turn the proxy on, as Put your server behind a reverse proxy shows. Then check the farm's certificate for the domain: under [manager_signature] it reads [manager_ca_signed], and its [manager_visibility] is [manager_public_in_token], as Use your own domain sets it up. Keys then carry the domain, and apps look it up.
items.proxy_hide: To send every app through the proxy, take the server's own addresses out of the keys:
items.proxy_step_mode: Edit each address, and set its [manager_mode] to [manager_private].
items.proxy_step_listen: Leave its [manager_listen] at [manager_yes], so the server keeps listening: the proxy still connects to it.
items.shot_proxy_alt: The Access Points of a server in VpnHood! MANAGER, set for a reverse proxy: Automatic Configuration off (1), and each address with Mode Private (2) and Listen Yes (3)
items.shot_proxy_caption: Both of the server's addresses are out of the keys, and the server still listens on them.
items.proxy_ca: MANAGER allows keys without an address only while the certificate reads [manager_ca_signed].
items.proxy_keys: Apps holding an older key keep using it, and the server's addresses with it: [manager_push_token] sends apps a new key only while one of the farm's servers has a [manager_public_in_token] address. Copy the new keys from MANAGER and give them to your users.
items.proxy_keep: Left at [manager_public_in_token], the addresses stay in the keys, and apps use them and the proxy alike. The proxy then keeps your users connected when an address is blocked.
items.proxy_farm: The domain leads to one server, so in a farm of several servers, every app that comes through the proxy reaches the same one.
items.next_domain: Use your own domain with a trusted certificate
